court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
title: Shishir Jain v. Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd.
one_line: A provisional assessment under Section 126(1) presupposes a lawful conclusion of unauthorised use, and no final assessment can be made or enforced — nor deposit compelled — without considering the consumer's objections and affording a personal hearing under Section 126(3) and Clause 8.1 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005.
facts_squib: A residential (LMV-1) connection at NOIDA was let out to working girls through Nestway Technologies; on inspection the licensee alleged a commercial girls' hostel was being run (billable under LMV-2), lodged an FIR under Section 135(1)(e), disconnected supply and raised a provisional assessment of Rs 1,74,725. After an earlier writ led to a 50% deposit and objections, the licensee served a 'final notice' treating the provisional figure as final without considering the objections or granting a hearing.
disposition: Writ petition allowed; the two impugned 'final' notices quashed as dehors Section 126 and Clause 8.1, with liberty to the licensee to complete a proper final assessment in accordance with law.
procedural_posture: Writ petition under Article 226 challenging the 'final' assessment notices
relief_granted: Impugned notices quashed; deposit of provisional amount cannot be compelled; liberty to reassess after objections and hearing.
consumer_category: residential connection alleged put to commercial (hostel) use
amendment_considered: post-2007 (Act 26 of 2007) — current Section 126 and the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 (Clause 8.1(b)(iv) references '2 (two) times the rates')

regulations_construed.reg: U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, Clause 8.1(b) (inspection, provisional assessment, show-cause/hearing and final assessment procedure for theft/UUE)

provision_holdings.holding: The condition precedent to a provisional assessment under Section 126(1) is a conclusion by the Assessing Officer that the person is indulging in unauthorised use; that satisfaction cannot rest on the officer's mere 'vagaries' without a fair opportunity of hearing in defence.
provision_holdings.key_para: the condition precedent to the provisional assessment under Section 126(1) is a conclusion by the Assessing Officer that the person concerned is indulged with unauthorized use of electricity. Such satisfaction cannot be permitted to be recorded on the mere vagaries of the Assessing Officer unless a fair opportunity of hearing in defence before the said authority is provided.

provision_holdings.holding: Principles of natural justice apply to proceedings for unauthorised use of electricity (which may in some cases also amount to an investigation under Section 135) unless excluded by the Act expressly or by necessary implication.
provision_holdings.key_para: It is well settled that principles of natural justice, unless excluded by the act in question or by necessary implication cannot be held to be inapplicable when a person is being indulged to the charge like unauthorized use of electric energy, which may, in some cases, also amount to investigation under Section 135 of the Act.

provision_holdings.holding: A final assessment made without considering the consumer's objections and without a personal hearing (as required by Section 126(3) and Clause 8.1(b)(iii) of the 2005 Code) is dehors the statutory provision and cannot stand.
provision_holdings.key_para: procedure prescribed under Section 126 of the Electricity Act, 2003 and in Clause 8.1 of the 2005 Code issuing provisional assessment bill has not been followed at all as no opportunity was given to the petitioner for personal hearing nor there is anything on record to reflect that the objection filed by him was taken into consideration at all. Thus, the entire procedure adopted by the respondent is dehors the statutory provision.

provision_holdings.holding: Absent a lawful final assessment made after considering objections and hearing, the consumer cannot be compelled to deposit the provisional amount.
provision_holdings.key_para: Without making final assessment after considering the objection and giving opportunity to the petitioner, he cannot be compelled to deposit any amount.

authorities.name: Ashok Kumar v. State of U.P.
authorities.principle: Natural justice / prescribed procedure must be followed before final assessment under Section 126.
authorities.treatment_para: The view being taken by us is fortified by various Division Bench jugments of this Court in the case of Ashok Kumar and others Vs. State of U.P. and others 2008(6) ADJ 660(DB), Kamil Vs. State of U.P. and others 2016(6) ADJ 11(DB)  and Hazi Mohd. Yaseen Vs. Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Limited 2011(10) ADJ 261(DB).

authorities.name: Kamil v. State of U.P.
authorities.principle: Same effect on the mandatory hearing/procedure before final assessment.

authorities.name: Hazi Mohd. Yaseen v. Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd.
authorities.principle: Same effect on the mandatory hearing/procedure before final assessment.

ratio.proposition: A Section 126 assessment is subject to natural justice: the provisional assessment presupposes a lawful conclusion of unauthorised use, and a final assessment (or any coerced deposit) is invalid unless the consumer's objections are considered and a personal hearing given, per Section 126(3) and Clause 8.1 of the 2005 Supply Code.

significance: An Allahabad Division-Bench authority quashing a 'final' assessment that was really a coerced provisional demand: it holds that Section 126(1) satisfaction of unauthorised use cannot rest on the officer's 'vagaries', that natural justice governs Section 126/135 proceedings unless excluded, and that no deposit can be compelled without a lawful final assessment made after objections and hearing under Section 126(3) and Clause 8.1 of the U.P. Supply Code. Useful on provisional-vs-final assessment and the natural-justice content of Section 126(3).

per_issue.natural-justice: good-law; consistent with the settled audi alteram partem requirement in Section 126(3) and the cited Allahabad DB line.
per_issue.provisional-final: good-law on the distinction between provisional and final assessment and the bar on coerced deposit.

validity.note: Not overruled. Applies the post-2007 Section 126 and the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005.
